question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Retire through Ownership Act (S 2403)
plain_language: This bill lets an employee stock-ownership plan rely on an independent appraiser's value for company stock that is not publicly traded, if the appraiser follows Internal Revenue Service methods. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Faster Labor Contracts Act (H R 5408)
plain_language: This bill establishes mandatory deadlines for parties negotiating an initial collective bargaining agreement and provides for mediation and arbitration to finalize those agreements. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act (H R 2988)
bill_title: Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act
plain_language: This bill modifies the requirements for fiduciaries of employer-sponsored retirement plans. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Recommit — Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act (H R 2988)
bill_title: Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act
plain_language: H.R. 2988 (Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act) modifies the requirements for fiduciaries of employer-sponsored retirement plans. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 2988)
bill_title: Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act
plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 2988 (Protecting Prudent Investment of Retirement Savings Act) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment requires the Government Accountability Office to publish a study on brokerage accounts.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Recommit — Tipped Employee Protection Act (H R 2312)
plain_language: H.R. 2312 (Tipped Employee Protection Act) modifies the definition of a tipped employee under the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to exclude consideration of an employee's duties when determining if the employee is a tipped employee. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

question: On Motion to Recommit — Empowering Employer Child and Elder Care Solutions Act (H R 2270)
bill_title: Empowering Employer Child and Elder Care Solutions Act
plain_language: H.R. 2270 (Empowering Employer Child and Elder Care Solutions Act) excludes the value of employer-funded child or dependent care from being used in calculating an eligible employee's overtime pay. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

question: On Passage — Flexibility for Workers Education Act (H R 2262)
plain_language: This bill modifies the definition of hours worked under the Fair Labor Standards Act to exclude certain voluntary training that occurs outside an employee's regular working hours. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.
